title: Stoneware Baked Spaghetti with Ground Beef & Hidden Vegetables
description: A hearty baked spaghetti with ground beef and finely chopped vegetables that blend right into the sauce. Baking everything together in stoneware gives the pasta a rich, casserole-style finish, while carrots, celery, and onion add flavor, moisture, and extra vegetables without taking over the dish.
ingredients: 1 jar (25 oz) 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce
1/2 tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
optionalTopping: 2-4 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese or 2-4 tbsp crushed pork rinds
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 F. Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente; it will finish cooking in the oven. Drain well and set aside.

Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it apart as it cooks. Drain excess fat if needed. Add the onion, celery, and carrots and continue cooking until the vegetables are tender and beginning to brown.

Pour the entire jar of 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce into the skillet. Add the garlic powder, oregano or Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the meat and vegetable sauce and toss until evenly coated. Lightly grease a large stoneware baking dish, transfer the spaghetti mixture to the dish, and spread evenly.

If desired, sprinkle the top with grated Parmesan cheese or crushed pork rinds. Cover with foil and bake at 375 F for 25-30 minutes, until hot throughout. Remove the foil and, for a lightly browned top, broil for 2-3 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning.
Let the baked spaghetti rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: Grating the carrots and finely chopping the celery and onion helps them blend into the meat sauce while contributing flavor and moisture.
Slightly undercook the spaghetti during the initial boil so it does not become overly soft during baking.
This recipe uses a full 25 oz jar of 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce.
This recipe is designed for a large stoneware baking dish. A comparable large casserole dish may also be used.
Parmesan adds a cheesy finish, while crushed pork rinds add texture and crunch.

breakdown: 12 oz Al Dente Protein Spaghetti: ~720-750 calories
25 oz 365 by Whole Foods Market Four Cheese Pasta Sauce: ~360-420 calories
